samples.summary: The frontend YorkieDocStore's copy of the five new attribute bands (listLevel, rowHeights, fontSize, cell padding, image size) has no test asserting a poisoned attribute is banded
samples.evidence: The diff adds normalizeListLevel/normalizeRowHeight/normalizeFontSize/normalizeCellPadding/isPaintableImageSize calls into packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts (lines ~195, ~215, ~320, ~470, ~512) — the live collaborative read path. The only tests that exercise a poisoned value are in packages/docs (test/model/list-level.test.ts, numeric-attrs.test.ts, row-height.test.ts) and they go through the *docs* package's own treeNodeToBlock, not this duplicated frontend parser. Grep of packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts for listLevel/rowHeights/fontSize/padding/image.width shows only well-formed values (e.g. listLevel: 0/1, fontSize: 14/18/20) — no 'Infinity', '1e9', 'NaN' or negative attribute anywhere. Because the frontend has no tsc lane and the two parsers are separate hand-written copies, a divergence (or a later revert) in this copy would ship undetected, re-enabling exactly the hang/page-flood this change exists to prevent.
searchedFor: grep NaN|Infinity across packages/frontend tests for docs store

samples.summary: The new non-termination guard for a degenerate pageSetup (`if (!(fragHeight > 0)) fragHeight = remaining;`) and the `contentHeight <= 0` branch of `paginatableRowHeight` are never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: pagination.ts:178 is added specifically for the `contentHeight <= 0` case, where line 171 would otherwise produce a non-positive fragment and walk `consumed` backwards forever; paginatableRowHeight (line ~82) likewise has an untested `if (!(contentHeight > 0)) return raw;` branch. Every new pagination test uses DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP: test/model/row-height.test.ts ('paginateLayout terminates on an unbounded row height') and test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts ('paginateLayout bounds a content-derived row height') both build `setup = DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP`, so contentHeight is ~864 and the new guard branch never runs. Existing test/view/pagination.test.ts comments confirm contentHeight = 864, and the largest margins in the suite (editor-page-setup.test.ts:319, margins 500/500) still leave positive content height and do not call paginateLayout on a table. So the one branch that stands between a malformed pageSetup and an infinite loop (a hung tab) has zero coverage.
searchedFor: read test/model/row-height.test.ts and numeric-attrs.test.ts pagination blocks

samples.summary: `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` has no direct unit test; its header/footer table-cell path — the stated reason for using it over `layout.blockParentMap` — and its `undefined` (block not in document) result are uncovered
samples.evidence: siblingBlocksOf is a new public model API. A repo grep finds no reference to it in any test file (only src/model/document.ts, src/view/editor.ts, src/view/text-editor.ts and a task doc). Coverage is only indirect via test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts, which covers a *body* table cell, a body cell missing from blockParentMap, and a stale table id. The doc comment on editor.ts:1659 and text-editor.ts:2909 justifies the model lookup precisely because a caret in a header/footer table cell resolves to undefined in the body layout's parent map — yet the only header test ('a header list carries its children too') uses top-level header blocks, not a header table cell. Nothing covers the footer walk (document.ts:327) or the `?? [block]` fallback, so a regression there would silently turn indent/outdent in a header/footer table list into a no-op with no test failing.

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (the plural array helper) is newly exported with no test and no caller
samples.evidence: packages/docs/test/model/row-height.test.ts tests only `normalizeRowHeight` (singular) plus the CRDT/layout/pagination paths; a repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeights` matches only its definition at row-height.ts:42. Nothing exercises it, so if it were ever adopted its behavior (position preservation, per-entry banding) is unverified.

samples.summary: The poisoned-listLevel normalizations added at the paint/PDF sites (paint-layout, doc-canvas, table-renderer, peer-cursor, pdf-painter) have no test with a non-finite or out-of-band level
samples.evidence: list-level.test.ts covers the CRDT boundary, computeListCounters, table-layout and the markdown serializer, but grep for NaN|Infinity across packages/docs/test/view matches only text-box-editor.test.ts, decoration-index.test.ts and editor-page-setup.test.ts — none of the list-marker painters. So the new normalizeListLevel calls in view/paint-layout.ts:199, view/doc-canvas.ts:600, view/table-renderer.ts:526, view/peer-cursor.ts:255/395 and export/pdf-painter.ts:370/593 are only covered for in-band levels (render-list-marker.test.ts, table-renderer.test.ts, pdf-exporter.test.ts). A regression at any of them (NaN marker x → invisible marker, NaN Map key in table-renderer's counter reset, NaN coordinates handed to pdf-lib) would not fail a test.
searchedFor: read test/model/list-level.test.ts 'poisoned listLevel at the raw readers' block

samples.summary: The text-box editor's new `doc.batch()` wrapping of indent/outdent is untested — only the resulting levels are asserted, not that the subtree is one undo unit
samples.evidence: The docs editor gets a TracingStore in test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts that asserts writeDepths === [1,1] and that one undo restores the whole subtree with canUndo() === false. The text-box equivalent (test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts, 'indent / outdent carry a list item's nested children') only checks the committed listLevels are [1,2]; nothing asserts the writes happened inside a batch or that a single undo reverses the whole subtree. If the batch were dropped there, Slides/Board users would get a half-moved subtree on one Cmd+Z and every existing assertion would still pass.
searchedFor: read the new text-box-editor.test.ts indent/outdent test in the diff

samples.summary: MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN clipping is only asserted as a page-count bound (`<= 202`); nothing checks the emitted fragments stay coherent when a row is clipped
samples.evidence: Both new pagination suites assert only `result.pages.length <= 202` / `<= 16`. That bound proves termination but holds for almost any bug that shortens the loop (e.g. a fragment of the wrong height, rowSplitOffset/rowSplitHeight that no longer tile the row, or a row silently dropped). No assertion inspects the produced PageLine rowSplitOffset/rowSplitHeight values or that the clipped row is still placed on the page, so a clipping regression would pass.
searchedFor: read the new pagination tests in test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts and row-height.test.ts

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real — I enumerated every paginateLayout call site in the test tree (pagination.test.ts, table-row-split.test.ts, table-origin-y.test.ts, decoration-index.test.ts, image-selection-tint.test.ts, serialize/json.test.ts, row-height.test.ts, numeric-attrs.test.ts, export/pdf-painter.test.ts, export/pdf-font-fallback.test.ts, packages/cli) and none passes a setup with contentHeight <= 0, so pagination.ts:178 and the `!(contentHeight > 0)` branch at pagination.ts:81 are indeed unexercised. But it is not blocking under this lens. (1) The behavior the diff actually adds is covered by non-vacuous tests: row-height.test.ts:89-110 paginates rowHeights of Infinity/1e9/NaN/-1e9 and asserts termination via pages.length <= 16, and numeric-attrs.test.ts:150-190 does the same for content-derived heights — the MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN bound and the non-finite handling in paginatableRowHeight are genuinely exercised. (2) The claimed impact (infinite loop / hung tab) is unreachable in production: every caller of paginateLayout resolves the setup first (editor.ts:1547+1571, pdf-exporter.ts:96+108, packages/cli/src/docs/paginate.ts:27+35), and resolvePageSetup (types.ts:865-896 with fitMargins types.ts:823-837) provably leaves a strictly positive content box — margins that would close it are scaled down to leave MIN_CONTENT_PX, and the total===0 / sub-pixel-page cases return zero margins over a positive paper size. That clamp has its own coverage (types.test.ts:92-129) and the deliberate write path throws RangeError on closed boxes (editor-page-setup.test.ts:198-243). So the uncovered residue is a defense-in-depth branch behind a separately tested invariant: minor coverage narrowness, not a gap that can let a user-visible or data-affecting defect ship.
